To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a combination prevention package, including home-based voluntary HIV testing and counseling, ART for HIV-infected individuals, and community mobilization, could be highly effective in reducing population-level HIV incidence, and that a large-scale trial is needed to test this hypothesis.

a combination prevention package, including home-based voluntary counseling and testing, and antiretrovival treatment for HIV-infected individuals, is predicted to reduce HIV population-level transmission substantially.

the HPTN 072 (PopART) intervention package could reduce HIV population level incidence by >60%, over three years, and that this reduction is mainly driven by the ART component of the intervention package, which will be delivered in both intervention arms.

the development of a novel combination intervention for HIV prevention.

the development of a novel approach to the control of HIV/AIDS, based upon the concept of treatment as prevention, and its application to a major epidemic.
